stages.title: Find where contact fails
stages.quote: The first trial kept the robot upright and lifted the stand, but the stand slipped from the one-handed grasp during lowering. I’m testing a second grasp lower on the pole to improve tilt control and prevent that drop.
stages.description: The first controller lifts the stand with one hand but loses contact during lowering. The agent adds a second grasp lower on the pole to resist tilt.
quote_excerpts: The first trial kept the robot upright and lifted the stand, but the stand slipped from the one-handed grasp during lowering. I’m testing a second grasp lower on the pole to improve tilt control and prevent that drop.

stages.title: Stabilize the grasp
stages.quote: The two-handed trial avoided the drop and reduced mean orientation error to about 12.5°. Position error remains about 17 cm because the robot lags behind the target and the arms run out of reach. I’m now testing body-tracking corrections while keeping the validated starting posture and grasp.
stages.description: The lower, second contact prevents the earlier drop. The remaining error comes from body lag: the arms approach their reach limit as the stand moves ahead.
stages.tag: Recover reach through body and arm motion
quote_excerpts: The two-handed trial avoided the drop and reduced mean orientation error to about 12.5°. Position error remains about 17 cm because the robot lags behind the target and the arms run out of reach. I’m now testing body-tracking corrections while keeping the validated starting posture and grasp.

stages.title: Bring the body into the motion
stages.quote: Position error remains about 17 cm because the robot lags behind the target and the arms run out of reach. I’m now testing body-tracking corrections while keeping the validated starting posture and grasp.
stages.description: The agent uses root-position error to adjust body lean, keeping the same two-handed grasp. Tracking improves, but the stand still finishes short of its target; the next revision adds a stronger correction and a standing hold.
stages.tag: Recover reach through body and arm motion
quote_excerpts: Position error remains about 17 cm because the robot lags behind the target and the arms run out of reach. I’m now testing body-tracking corrections while keeping the validated starting posture and grasp.

stages.title: Complete the carry
stages.quote: Freezing the unnecessary body motion near the end improved the full-curve result to 6.3 cm mean ADD, 5.1 cm mean position error, and 7.4° mean orientation error. The robot remains upright and the stand reaches the endpoint area under control. I’m refining the remaining pose offset and testing release onto the floor.
stages.description: Body tracking and a standing hold bring the stand through the carry. The hands remain in contact at the end; a controlled release is still needed.
stages.tag: Coordinate whole-body control and arm control
quote_excerpts: Freezing the unnecessary body motion near the end improved the full-curve result to 6.3 cm mean ADD, 5.1 cm mean position error, and 7.4° mean orientation error. The robot remains upright and the stand reaches the endpoint area under control. I’m refining the remaining pose offset and testing release onto the floor.

stages.title: Place and release
stages.quote: I’m saving the tested controller with the longer settling interval. … The robot stayed upright, and the stand was motionless and fully floor-supported with no robot contact during the last second.
stages.description: The controller opens the fingers over one second and withdraws the hands sideways. A two-second settling interval confirms that the stand remains floor-supported after contact ends.
quote_excerpts: I’m saving the tested controller with the longer settling interval.
The robot stayed upright, and the stand was motionless and fully floor-supported with no robot contact during the last second.
